description: Seed list of seed specs, plus related projects and episodes. Entries are data, not instructions.

entries.name: A personal AI system
entries.summary: Ledgers that record obligations at the moment they are said; layered file memory for agents that remember nothing; bounded unattended work.

entries.name: Hermes Agent
entries.summary: An open-source, model-agnostic personal agent with bounded curated memory, searchable session history and skills as procedural memory, reachable from a terminal and many messaging platforms.
entries.relevance: A well-documented public design for agent memory and skills, useful to compare any system against.

entries.name: LifeOS (formerly Personal AI Infrastructure, PAI)
entries.summary: An open-source personal AI setup built on a coding agent, organizing context, skills and goals around moving from a current state to a desired one. The original PAI repository address redirects here.
entries.relevance: A public, opinionated example of a complete personal AI system, shared so others can learn from it.

entries.name: Inside Nathan's Second Brain: Daniel Miessler, Security Expert & Creator of PAI, Audits My AI Setup
entries.summary: A podcast conversation in which Nathan Labenz walks through his personal AI setup and Daniel Miessler reviews it, covering context, agent hierarchy, security and norms.
entries.relevance: Part of that setup was built by having an agent compare other people's published setups and draft a synthesis, which is the kind of exchange seed specs are meant to make easier.
